shihtzu: The Shih Tzu originated in Tibet and was further developed in China as a royal lap dog. Its name translates to "Lion Dog" in Mandarin Chinese, reflecting its bred resemblance to the lions seen in traditional Asian art and Buddhist mythology.
frenchbulldog: The French Bulldog originated in England as a toy-size version of the Bulldog. They were popular with lace workers in Nottingham, who then emigrated to France during the Industrial Revolution, taking their dogs with them where the breed was further refined.
labrador: The Labrador Retriever originated in Newfoundland, Canada. Originally known as the St. John's water dog, they were bred to help fishermen haul nets, fetch ropes, and retrieve fish that escaped from the nets.
retriever: The Golden Retriever originated in the Scottish Highlands in the late 19th century. They were bred by Dudley Marjoribanks, 1st Baron Tweedmouth, by crossing a Yellow Retriever with the now-extinct Tweed Water Spaniel to create an ideal gundog for retrieving waterfowl.
germanshepherd: The German Shepherd originated in Germany in 1899. They were originally bred for herding and guarding sheep, developed by Max von Stephanitz who wanted to create a standardized German herding dog.
poodle: The Poodle originated in Germany as a water retriever, although it was later standardized in France. The breed's name comes from the German word "Pudel," which means "to splash in water."
dachshund: The Dachshund originated in Germany where they were bred to hunt badgers, rabbits, and other burrowing animals. Their name translates literally to "badger dog" in German.
bulldog: The Bulldog originated in England and was originally bred for the bloody sport of bull-baiting in the 13th century. After the sport was outlawed in 1835, the breed was preserved and bred to have a gentler, more affectionate temperament.
beagle: The Beagle originated in England. While small hounds of similar type existed for centuries, the modern breed was developed in Great Britain around the 1830s for hunting hare, known as beagling.
rottweiler: The Rottweiler originated in Germany, specifically in the town of Rottweil. They are one of the oldest of herding breeds, with roots tracing back to Roman times when they were used to drive cattle and pull carts for butchers.
pointer: The English Pointer originated in England in the 1600s. They were bred to "point" at birds and small game, assisting hunters long before the invention of firearms when hunting was done with nets.
pembroke: The Pembroke Welsh Corgi originated in Pembrokeshire, Wales. They were bred for herding cattle, sheep, and horses, and are famously associated with British royalty, particularly Queen Elizabeth II.
corgi: Corgis originated in Wales and were traditionally used as herding dogs. They are divided into two distinct breeds: the Pembroke Welsh Corgi and the Cardigan Welsh Corgi.
husky: The Siberian Husky originated in Northeast Asia, developed by the Chukchi people of Siberia for sled pulling and companionship. They were brought to Nome, Alaska in 1908 to serve as working sled dogs.
shiba: The Shiba Inu originated in Japan. It is the smallest of the six original and distinct spitz breeds of dog native to Japan, originally bred for hunting small game and birds in mountainous terrain.
samoyed: The Samoyed originated in Siberia and Northwest Russia. They take their name from the Samoyedic peoples of Siberia, who bred these fluffy white dogs to herd reindeer and pull sleds.
pug: The Pug originated in China, dating back to the Han dynasty (B.C. 206 to A.D. 200). They were bred to be companion dogs for the Chinese ruling families and lived in luxury.
chihuahua: The Chihuahua originated in Mexico and is named after the Mexican state of Chihuahua. They are believed to be descendants of the Techichi, a companion dog favored by the Toltec civilization.
boxer: The Boxer originated in Germany in the late 19th century. They were bred from the now-extinct Bullenbeisser (a mastiff-type dog) and Bulldogs brought in from Great Britain, originally used for hunting large game.
greatdane: The Great Dane originated in Germany, despite its English name. Originally known as the Boarhound or German Mastiff, they were bred by German nobles for hunting wild boar.
akita: The Akita originated in the mountainous regions of northern Japan. They were originally bred to hunt large game such as wild boar, elk, and the Yezo bear, and are considered a national treasure in Japan.
malamute: The Alaskan Malamute originated in Alaska, named after the Mahlemut (now known as Kuuvangmiut) Iñupiaq people of the Norton Sound region. They are one of the oldest Arctic sled dogs.
dalmatian: The Dalmatian is widely believed to have originated in Dalmatia, a historic region of Croatia. They have served many roles throughout history, notably as carriage dogs and later famously as firehouse mascots.
chow: The Chow Chow originated in northern China, where it is known as Songshi Quan (meaning "puffy-lion dog"). It is an ancient breed that was used for hunting, herding, and guarding.
pekinese: The Pekingese originated in China as a companion dog for Chinese royalty. They could only be owned by members of the Chinese Imperial Palace and were considered sacred.
pomeranian: The Pomeranian originated in the Pomerania region (now part of Poland and Germany) in Central Europe. They were bred down in size from larger Spitz-type sled dogs and gained massive popularity after Queen Victoria acquired one.
mastiff: The English Mastiff originated in Britain. These giant working dogs have an ancient lineage, having been used as guard dogs and for fighting alongside British soldiers against Roman legions.
collie: The Collie originated in the Scottish Highlands and Northern England, where they were bred as sheep-herding dogs. Their name likely comes from "colley," the Scottish word for a black-faced sheep.
